notes: The previous off-ramp spillback capacity was not a physical Vissim storage value. It came from storage capacity plus three downstream movement capacities.
For this Vissim network the downstream approach space is shared, so summing every turning movement overcounts available storage.
The first v2 provisional value of 240 veh per model off-ramp was still too high when checked against actual Vissim connector/stem lane-metres.
This revised v2 uses direction-specific connector-plus-stem-to-signal physical storage estimates from the INPX geometry audit.
Freeway segment lengths, ordinary urban storage, boundary output storage, and on-ramp storage are now Vissim geometry based.
Signal q_sat/lost_time remain scalar engineering fallbacks because the per-approach signal regression is not robustly identified.
F ramp metering is guarded as invalid for physical metering calibration; it should stay always-green/monitor-only unless explicitly overridden for diagnostics.

2026-07-14: re-derived for the 8-seg extended mainline (modi_eval_vsl_8seg.inpx); only the freeway segment length profile changed vs v2_onramp_route_20260630 — storage/ramp/urban capacities are link-based and unchanged by the resegmentation.

D_offramp_stem.name: D trumpet stem DT to D

F_offramp_stem.name: F trumpet stem FT to F

freeway_segment_length_source.note: 8-seg corridor lengths (segment_end_m - segment_start_m, corridor coordinates). S0 includes the entry extension link + 4 m gap connector; S7 includes the main-link tail + 4 m gap connector + exit extension link. Base: v2_onramp_route_20260630.

urban_link_storage_capacity_source.method: storage_veh = effective_length_m * lane_count / jam_spacing. Signal-controlled internal approaches use stopline position; outbound boundary links and links ending at uncontrolled E use full link length.

on_ramp_storage_capacity_source.method: Per-direction model reservoir assumes one Vissim ramp lane per direction up to the ramp-meter signal head: D 160.883 m, F 256.326 m.

boundary_queue_capacity_source.method: Scalar fallback uses the largest inbound boundary stopline storage among 2-lane boundary approaches: 478 m * 2 / 6.49.
boundary_queue_capacity_source.note: Boundary queue is mainly diagnostic/compatibility in detector-local mode.

ramp_queue_capacity_source.method: Scalar fallback uses the largest one-lane on-ramp pre-meter storage, F: 256.326 m / 6.49.
ramp_queue_capacity_source.note: Core Numerical-Sim currently has only one ramp_queue_max_veh scalar; per-ramp queue maxima should be promoted into core config later.

network.rho_max_note: Observed max density only; do not treat as calibrated jam density yet.

ramp_metering.F_note: F ramp remains discharge-limited despite sustained queue under route bias. Treat as network route/lane/connector issue before using for controller calibration.

signal.note: 15-sec burst max rates are not used directly. The median fitted value is low because several approaches are underfed; use 1800 vph/approach as a conservative initial controller value and refine with detector/output-based saturated approach runs.

urban_mfd.production_proxy_note: Production is measured as aggregated signal stop-line discharge, not completed trips.

observation.metric_scope_note: These split fractions calibrate ONLY the local detector queue<->storage decomposition. They are NOT a total-mass/propagation calibration and must not be mixed with route/turning-split or controller-objective tuning. The 0.90/0.20 grid fit improved storage(-47%) and movement-queue(-40%) decomposition but worsened total_model_vehicles(+14.5%); see evaluation/runs/observation_split_grid_refined_20260629. During controller validation, total_model_vehicles MUST be reported and judged separately from protected_accumulation_veh / urban_link_occupancy_total_veh / urban_movement_queue_total_veh.
observation.fit_basis: Saved Vissim state replay over held-out no-control profiles ramp_d_bias, fw_eb_heavy, and urban_d_heavy. Candidate split values were scored by weighted relative one-step prediction MAE for total vehicles, protected accumulation, urban queue+storage, urban storage, and urban movement queue.
observation.note: This promotion targets local detector queue/storage decomposition, not total vehicle mass. Combined urban queue+storage and total model vehicle errors should still be read separately during controller validation.

route_bias_forecast.status_note: Demoted from promoted_20260629 on 2026-06-29 audit follow-up: the 0.98 on-ramp-arrival approximation was promoted on a forecast-value sanity check only, with no measured held-out prediction-error improvement. VISSIM d/f_ramp_bias changes static route RelFlow(1)=100/0.01 across all routing decisions (run_stackelberg_vissim_controller.vbs:559-605), not VehicleInput volumes; the forecast still keeps total ramp demand fixed and leaves urban turn/off-ramp splits static. Keep candidate until evaluation/runs/audit_followup_20260629/route_bias_onoff_replay shows component-error improvement.

v2_candidate.schema: Set route_bias_forecast.version=2 and supply v2={target_multiplier, cross_share, off_share, direction_feed} to activate the direction-aware forecast in profiled_demand_rates (adapter). v2 loads only the direction-feeding ramp (d_ramp_bias -> R_D_W/FW_W, f_ramp_bias -> R_F_E/FW_E) with target_multiplier x ramp_vph, gives the same-node cross ramp cross_share, and starves the other node off_share. Total ramp demand is not preserved.
v2_candidate.finding: v2 is conceptually more correct than v1 (direction-aware, magnitude untied from hardcoded ramp_vph) but does NOT robustly reduce held-out one-step prediction error. The one-step prediction is insensitive to the ramp-arrival forecast; the large protected/urban errors are driven by urban turn/off-ramp splits. Do not promote v2 until a live VISSIM A/B fits the urban turning/off-ramp split. Best v2 multiplier in the sweep was ~1.0.

audit_followup_20260629.result: v1(0.98) ON does not improve held-out component error (f_ramp_bias got worse). Demoted to candidate.

route_bias_forecast.target_share_basis: Vissim route-bias profiles set static route relative flow to 100.0 for routes containing the target D/F ramp link and 0.01 otherwise; the model forecast approximates this as 98% of total on-ramp arrival assigned to the target D or F ramp pair while preserving total ramp demand.

candidate_bayesian_update_no_wu_pfo_10se.promotion_guard: Do not promote. This artifact used observed/already-calibrated-predicted ratios, not observed/raw-predicted ratios.

prediction.note: This v2 step stores calibrated one-step audit summaries and does not silently scale the controller's METANET propagation dynamics.

onramp_route_forecast.basis: VISSIM static routes send ~10.5% of each urban origin demand onto D(link25->R_D_W) and F(link31->R_F_E) on-ramps; ~1032 vph/dir at u1400 vs hardcoded 250/ramp.
